report:
Likely difference: Model B is more biased toward news/reportage-style language than Model A.

Why I think this:
- Across many high-norm cells (esp. deeper layers, positions 1–4), the logit-lens top tokens cluster around news domains: legal/government (“law,” “Law,” “wrong,” “incorrect”), medical/health (“surgeon,” “clinic,” “surgery,” “treatment”), economy/disasters (“downturn,” “tragic,” “tragedy”), and sports/proper nouns (“Royals,” “Manny,” “baseman,” “Herald”).
- Discourse/time markers typical of reportage show up repeatedly at pos1 (“Later,” “later,” “ago,” “latter,” “mention,” “visits”).
- The pos0 progression also leans into headline/section-title or article copy vocabulary (“Author,” “Best,” “Stay,” “Every,” “Consider,” “Sustainable,” “recommend,” “Do/Check/ensure/strive/adopt”), which fits news/editorial tone.

What I don’t see:
- Clear signatures of other specific objectives (e.g., safety disclaimers, code/math, chatty first-person RLHF tropes).

So, the evidence supports a domain shift: Model B appears more tuned toward news/media reporting (including health/legal and sports desks) relative to Model A.
